description: Basic reproduction number targeted when calibrating contact rates.
citation: Guerra et al. 2017, Lancet Infect Dis 17(12):e420-e428
notes: 15 is the midpoint of the 12-18 range in the abstract. Not a model argument: it enters through contact_rate (school) or the calibrated contact_matrix (mixing models). Projects may use other values.

description: Proportion immune needed to prevent sustained transmission (about 93%).
citation: Derived: 1 - 1/R0 with R0 = 15
notes: Standard formula. Used as the default prop_vaccinated in ModelMeaslesSchool().

description: Number of agents in the model.
citation: Scenario-specific input
notes: No default; set by each project.

description: Initial number (school) or proportion (mixing models) of infected agents.
citation: Scenario-specific input
notes: Default of 1 index case in ModelMeaslesSchool(); no default in the mixing models.

description: Proportion of the population vaccinated (immunized).
citation: Scenario-specific input; school default derived as 1 - 1/R0
notes: ModelMeaslesSchool() defaults to the herd-immunity threshold for R0 = 15; the mixing models have no default. Projects use local coverage data.

description: Probability of transmission per contact between an infectious and a susceptible agent.
citation: Assumption: highly transmissible; Utah DHHS Measles Disease Plan (updated March 26, 2026): "90% of susceptible contacts will develop disease"
notes: Fixed high, then the contact rate or contact matrix is calibrated to R0.

description: Average number of contacts per agent per day (school model).
citation: Calibrated to the target R0 = 15
notes: R0 = transmission_rate x contact_rate x prodromal_period, so the default is 15 / 0.9 / 4 = 4.17 contacts per day.

description: Expected number of contacts per day between population groups (mixing models).
citation: Calibrated to the target R0 with the next-generation-matrix method (Diekmann et al. 2010, J R Soc Interface 7(47):873-885)
notes: No default. Scale a contact structure with calibrate_mixing_model().

description: Reduction in contacts during the rash period (1 = full reduction, i.e. agents with rash stay home).
citation: Assumption

description: Average days from exposure to the start of the prodromal (infectious) period.
citation: Utah DHHS Measles Disease Plan (updated March 26, 2026): exposure to prodrome averages 8-12 days

description: Standard deviation of the incubation period, which is lognormal (drawn when the agent is infected).
citation: Lessler et al. 2009, Lancet Infect Dis 9(5):291-300: lognormal incubation period (exposure to first symptoms) with median 12.5 days and dispersion 1.23
notes: A dispersion of 1.23 is a coefficient of variation of 0.21, or 2.5 days at the default mean of 12 days (5th-95th percentiles 8.4-16.5 days). The fit's 5th-95th percentiles are 8.9-17.7 days. With a geometric incubation period of mean 12 days (before 0.4.1-0), 16% of cases were still latent after 21 days; with the lognormal, 0.2%.

description: Average days of the infectious prodromal period, before rash onset.
citation: Utah DHHS Measles Disease Plan (updated March 26, 2026): prodrome lasts 2-4 days (range 2-8); contagious 4 days before rash onset

description: Standard deviation of the prodromal period, which is lognormal (drawn at the start of the prodromal period).
citation: Fit to the 1861 Hagelloch outbreak (data in the R package surveillance, Meyer et al. 2017, J Stat Softw 77(11)): days from prodrome onset to rash onset in 188 cases, mean 3.95, sd 1.74
notes: Interval-censored fits: lognormal with mean 4.0 and sd 1.7 (AIC 695.7) and gamma with mean 4.0 and sd 1.6 (AIC 695.0) fit equally well; an exponential (geometric) duration fits much worse (AIC 887.7). The CDC Pink Book gives a prodrome of 2-4 days (range 1-7).

description: Average days of the infectious part of the rash period.
citation: Utah DHHS Measles Disease Plan (updated March 26, 2026): contagious to 4 days after rash onset; infectivity minimal after day 2 of rash
notes: The visible rash lasts 6-7 days; the model only tracks the infectious part.

description: Standard deviation of the infectious part of the rash period, which is lognormal (drawn at rash onset).
citation: Assumption
notes: Cases are considered contagious through 4 days after rash onset (Utah DHHS Measles Disease Plan), so the infectious part of the rash varies little. With the default mean of 3 days, 99% of rash periods last 1-6 days.

description: Efficacy of two doses of MMR vaccine.
citation: Utah DHHS Measles Disease Plan (updated March 26, 2026) ("~97%"); CDC
notes: Earlier versions used 0.99 (Liu et al. 2015, BMC Public Health 15:447, https://doi.org/10.1186/s12889-015-1766-6).

description: Vaccine reduction in recovery rate. Not active.
citation: Not active
notes: Registered by the C++ model as "(IGNORED) Vax improved recovery"; it has no effect on the simulation. ModelMeaslesSchool() no longer takes it.

description: Daily rate of hospitalization during the rash period (a rate, not a probability): each day with rash, an agent is hospitalized with this probability.
citation: Calibrated to 10% of cases hospitalized: CDC national data for 2026 (479 of 4,588 confirmed cases, about 10%, as of October 22, 2026); 8% overall (9% among unvaccinated) in Utah per Jones et al. 2026, NEJM Evid 5(8)
notes: Convert to a probability with p = 1 - E[(1 - h)^D], with D the rash period: 0.101 with the defaults. To target a probability p with a rash of D days, use h = 1 - (1 - p)^(1/D) (exact for a fixed rash period). Before 0.4.1-0 the default was 0.2 (an assumption) and, with a geometric rash period, p = h / (h + 1/rash_period) = 0.375. Jones et al. 2026: https://doi.org/10.1056/EVIDpha2600141. Wang et al. 2026, MMWR 75:252-257 (https://doi.org/10.15585/mmwr.mm7520a1) reports 18.5% in West Texas; 2025 national data showed 11-13%.

description: Average days in hospital.
citation: Assumption
notes: Observed stays are shorter: in Utah, a mean of 2.1 nights (range 0-7) (Jones et al. 2026); in West Texas, a median of 2 days (range 0-20) (Wang et al. 2026).

description: Average days from rash onset to detection by public health (detected cases are isolated and trigger quarantine).
citation: Assumption: about 2 days from active case to public health notification

description: Days a detected case stays in isolation.
citation: Utah DHHS Measles Disease Plan (updated March 26, 2026): isolate until 4 days after rash onset

description: Days an exposed susceptible agent stays in quarantine.
citation: Utah DHHS Measles Disease Plan (updated March 26, 2026): 21 days since last exposure

description: Quarantine days for high-risk contacts (tiered quarantine).
citation: Assumption
notes: Experimental; no published source. The 21-day tier matches the 21-day quarantine of the Utah DHHS Measles Disease Plan.

description: Quarantine days for medium-risk contacts (tiered quarantine).
citation: Assumption
notes: Experimental; no published source.

description: Quarantine days for low-risk contacts (tiered quarantine).
citation: Assumption
notes: Experimental; no published source.

description: Probability that an agent accepts quarantine.
citation: Assumption
notes: Some analyses use 0.9.

description: Probability that a detected case accepts isolation.
citation: Assumption
notes: Some analyses use 0.9.

description: Probability that a contact of a detected case is successfully traced.
citation: Assumption
notes: Some analyses use 0.8.

description: Days around rash onset during which contacts are traced.
citation: Assumption; matches the Utah DHHS Measles Disease Plan (updated March 26, 2026) exposure definition: 4 days before through 4 days after rash onset

description: Daily probability of detecting a prodromal agent while a quarantine is active.
citation: Assumption: on average, it takes about two days to detect a prodromal agent while a quarantine is active
notes: A daily probability of 0.5 gives an average of 2 days to detection.

description: Efficacy of MMR vaccine given as post-exposure prophylaxis.
notes: InterventionMeaslesPEP() has no defaults; value used in vignette("school").

description: Efficacy of immune globulin given as post-exposure prophylaxis.
citation: Assumption: set equal to MMR vaccine efficacy
notes: Consistent with Arciuolo et al. 2017 (100%, approx. CI 56.2-99.8) and Montroy et al. 2025, Vaccine 47:126706 (76-100%). Value used in vignette("school").

description: Days after exposure during which MMR is offered as PEP.
citation: Utah DHHS Measles Disease Plan (updated March 26, 2026): MMR within 72 hours
notes: Value used in vignette("school").

description: Days after exposure during which immune globulin is offered as PEP.
citation: Utah DHHS Measles Disease Plan (updated March 26, 2026): immune globulin within 6 days
notes: Value used in vignette("school").

description: Mean duration of immune globulin protection.
citation: Assumption within the 30-45-day range reported for measles antibody
notes: The CDC Pink Book interval table assumes 30 days. Value used in vignette("school").

description: Standard deviation of the duration of immune globulin protection.
citation: Assumption
notes: Value used in vignette("school").

description: Probability that an agent accepts MMR as PEP.
citation: Assumption
notes: Value used in vignette("school").

description: Probability that an agent accepts immune globulin as PEP.
citation: Assumption
notes: Value used in vignette("school").
